note: On four of five criteria this is the closest match to the stated ICP in the entire batch. Successful: owns a video production business, DP on a feature documentary, and separately runs a coaching programme for other filmmakers. Income: no affordability signal appeared in 48 minutes and the price reaction was the archetypal optimizer response — 'I wasn't expecting it to be this high, but absolutely respect him and his price' — with no attempt to negotiate. Good_to_great is his own language before the rep supplied any: 'what a shame to live a life and to never know your full capacity', 'If you're not growing, you're dying', 'I'm already in good shape, I run a solid business, I have good things going on, but personally I want more right now.' Not_deconditioned is emphatic — 32, 6'2", 190-195, nineteen years of lifting, five years of jiu-jitsu with two to three competing, plus Muay Thai and kickboxing across nine to ten sessions a week. The single miss is neglected_health, and it is the one that decided the call. Health is not the neglected corner of this man's life, it is the most developed one, which is why the rep concluded — correctly — that the coaching product did not fit and routed him to a $200/mo subscription. This is now the third instance in this batch, after Hamdi Hmimy and Paul Bionaz, of the same pattern: a prospect who satisfies the aspirational half of the stated ICP almost perfectly and fails on need. The stated definition screens on who someone is and not on whether the programme has anything to add, and it cannot detect this before the call is booked. Set against the corpus-level observation already in icp.json that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP, the more useful finding may be that it is also differently shaped: the people the ICP describes best are the ones being sold the cheapest product.
